Title: Session Hijacking / Spoofing
Threat_Scenario: Stolen or fixed customer session token is used to impersonate an active user account over the network.
Preconditions: Session id accessible via XSS or weak token generation entropy.
Proposed_Control: Enforce cryptographically random session tokens with secure flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite).

Title: Client-Side Price Manipulation
Threat_Scenario: Client modifies product price or order total parameters within the HTTP browser request before checkout.
Preconditions: Server implicitly trusts client-supplied price parameters during cart submission.
Proposed_Control: Enforce server-side price validation by looking up costs directly in database inventory tables.

Title: Unlogged Privileged Activity
Threat_Scenario: Privileged administrative refund or profile change lacks reliable actor attribution and non-repudiation evidence.
Preconditions: Audit logging framework fails to track user context during dynamic internal API routing calls.
Proposed_Control: Implement mandatory structured logging that binds the user ID to all state-changing activities.

Title: SQL Injection in Catalog Engine
Threat_Scenario: Unsafe query string construction exposes full customer or order database registries over the network.
Preconditions: User input is directly concatenated into database WHERE filtration clause components.
Proposed_Control: Mandate parameterized queries and prepared statements across all data extraction logic wrappers.
Evidence_Label: Simulated, informed by WEB-001 lab lesson

Title: Application Denial of Service
Threat_Scenario: Automated rapid-fire network requests exhaust application or relational database connection capacity.
Preconditions: No layer-7 limiters configured on edge proxy gateways or application worker frameworks.
Proposed_Control: Configure strict rate-limiting thresholds and connection throttling on public edge nodes.

Title: Administrative Function Bypassing
Threat_Scenario: Customer directly requests an administrative path to perform execution actions without validation.
Preconditions: Administrative endpoints rely strictly on hidden URLs instead of server-side role validation blocks.
Proposed_Control: Enforce centralized server-side authorization filters requiring verified admin security tokens.
Evidence_Label: Simulated, informed by WEB-003 lab lesson

Title: Reflected Script Injection
Threat_Scenario: Unencoded search input executes malicious JavaScript within another user's browser context.
Preconditions: Store search fields reflect parameter content back into the page layout without encoding tokens.
Proposed_Control: Apply contextual HTML entity output encoding rules to all dynamic parameters before rendering.
Evidence_Label: Simulated, informed by WEB-002 lab lesson

Title: Multi-Factor Step Circumvention
Threat_Scenario: Password-authenticated session directly accesses protected account dashboards before 2FA verification finishes.
Preconditions: The authentication engine tracks username strings but fails to validate MFA state across deep routes.
Proposed_Control: Implement explicit server-side state-locked workflow checks before serving private data dashboards.
Evidence_Label: Simulated, informed by WEB-004 lab lesson

Title: Webhook Forgery / Replay
Threat_Scenario: Forged or replayed Stripe payment status notifications alter order state strings without true collection.
Preconditions: Application processes inbound webhooks without verifying token provenance or unique request IDs.
Proposed_Control: Validate Stripe signature headers, verify timestamps, and enforce server-side event idempotency.

Title: Secret Exposure in Repository
Threat_Scenario: Plaintext secret committed to GitHub repo permits unauthorized cloud environment or database access.
Preconditions: Developers hardcode credentials locally within source code configuration files or layout playbooks.
Proposed_Control: Deploy automated push-blocking secret scanning tools and migrate to secure cloud environment variables.

Title: Log Injection and Blinding
Threat_Scenario: Security events are dropped, altered, or delayed mid-transit, preventing accurate log correlation.
Preconditions: Forwarders utilize unauthenticated connections or allow log file manipulation on the local volume layer.
Proposed_Control: Enforce authenticated log shipping channels and lock down CloudTrail using write-once policies.

Title: Excessive Privilege Access
Threat_Scenario: Support agent accesses more customer profiles or data rows than their operational role requires.
Preconditions: Application relies on broad data access scripts instead of mapping tight, field-level data masks.
Proposed_Control: Enforce granular, server-side data access rules and mask sensitive customer data fields.
